Credential note
One legacy Quarto source contained an API key directly in source code. That credential is intentionally not copied into this repository or this provenance note. If the historical credential has not already been revoked, it should be rotated. The reconstructed project reads credentials only from OPENAI_API_KEY and ignores .env in version control.

Current snapshot evidence
OpenAI currently documents gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 as the dated GPT-4 Turbo snapshot and lists Chat Completions support. It is marked deprecated. This makes it the best-supported dated snapshot for a controlled reconstruction, but it does not retroactively prove what serving state produced a preserved 2024 response. See BEREC_REPLICATION.md.

title: BEREC Reconstruction
text:
BEREC is analyzed separately from the principal five-PON model comparison.
The main comparison uses IRG, EUHC, cOAlition S, CAN, and CEER under a common reconstructed step-by-step (SBS) protocol. BEREC presents a different provenance problem: a preserved historical output exists, but the exact historical interaction cannot be reconstructed with sufficient confidence to treat a new run as an exact replication.
The BEREC analysis therefore compares three distinct conditions without treating any of them as ground truth.

title: BEREC Reconstruction
text:
Interpretation
The BEREC reconstruction provides useful evidence about the recoverability of the historical classification pattern. Under the best-evidenced December 23 configuration, the pinned GPT-4 Turbo snapshot reproduces 13 of the 15 classifications present in the preserved historical artifact.
That result should not be interpreted as an exact replication of the historical API interaction. The surviving evidence does not establish every element of the original BEREC request strongly enough to make that claim.
Likewise, the five differences between the reconstructed GPT-4 Turbo condition and the GPT-5.4 nano SBS condition cannot be attributed exclusively to model change. Those conditions differ in both model and reconstructed protocol.
For this reason, BEREC remains an auxiliary provenance and reconstruction analysis and is not added as a sixth organization to the principal five-PON model comparison.

title: SBS Model Comparison
text:
Main result
Across the 75 PON-question classifications, the frozen GPT-4 Turbo SBS responses agree with the confirmed human reference in 86.7% of cases.
GPT-5.4 nano agrees with the human reference in 78.7% of cases, a -8.0 percentage-point change relative to frozen GPT-4 Turbo. It changes 14 of 75 classifications (18.7%): 4 toward the human reference and 10 away.
GPT-5.6 Luna agrees with the human reference in 81.3% of cases, a -5.3 percentage-point change relative to frozen GPT-4 Turbo. It changes 12 of 75 classifications (16.0%): 4 toward the human reference and 8 away.
The results are descriptive of this fixed five-PON, 15-question comparison. They do not establish that one model is generally superior across other tasks, prompts, or domains.

title: Methods
text:
Reconstructed 2024 SBS protocol
The final Dec. 24 implementation used Chat Completions with:

a system message containing the policy-analyst instruction, the SBS suffix, and the ordered questions; and
a user message containing the complete boundary-object text.

The request supplied model and messages explicitly. No temperature, top-p, token limit, seed, response format, or tools were explicitly supplied in the historical code.
The recovered base instruction is:

You are a policy analyst focused on extracting organizational features from documents that regulate the organization and functioning of specific organizations. I will provide the documents and a list of yes-no questions. You will only return TRUE or FALSE responses according to the list of yes-no questions, including a row with the question itself. The output must be in CSV format.

The manuscript-facing SBS condition appends:

Let’s think step by step

The project preserves the recovered string-concatenation behavior, including its whitespace quirks. scripts/00_check_protocol.py prints the resulting prompt hash without making an API call.

title: Methods
text:
Human coders and majority vote
The authoritative human file is input/reference/legacy_human_responses_confirmed.csv. The individual coders are displayed as HBM, ASC, and JNG.
For each question/PON combination, the pipeline records:

each individual human response;
the three-human majority vote, used as the confirmed human reference;
whether the human coders are unanimous; and
each model classification and whether it agrees with that human majority.

Historical four-coder agreement is expressed with explicit counts such as 3 TRUE / 1 FALSE rather than the manuscript’s shorthand. The original 1, 0, 3-1, 2-2, and 3-1* values are retained only as manuscript-reference fields.

title: Methods
text:
Frozen historical benchmark
The five *_sbs.txt files from Dec. 24, 2024 are treated as immutable research artifacts. The principal runner refuses gpt-4-turbo and gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09, preventing accidental regeneration through the contemporary-model workflow.

title: Methods
text:
Contemporary-model runs
The principal comparison registers two contemporary arms: the pinned GPT-5.4 nano snapshot gpt-5.4-nano-2026-03-17 and GPT-5.6 Luna using the currently exposed API model ID gpt-5.6-luna. Each arm was executed independently with scripts/03_run_current_model.py, using five requests—one per strict-comparison PON—and writing only to its own timestamped directory under output/current/. Completed runs are discovered and reused, so the current comparison does not rerun GPT-5.4 nano, GPT-5.6 Luna, or any historical output.
Each response receives a JSON metadata sidecar. A fully successful run receives run_manifest.json with status: complete; if execution fails after the run directory is created, partial outputs are retained and run_failed.json records the failure. Downstream comparison scripts accept only runs whose completion manifest explicitly reports status == "complete" and require one completed run for every model registered in comparison.comparison_models. OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Luna model page was checked on 2026-08-31: its Snapshots section listed gpt-5.6-luna but no dated snapshot identifier. The project therefore treats gpt-5.6-luna as an undated model ID, records the documentation URL and check date in configuration, and preserves the UTC execution time plus requested and API-returned model IDs in response metadata and the run manifest. It is not described as a dated or immutable snapshot.

title: Methods
text:
BEREC replication boundary
The original BEREC Dec. 23 request state is not recoverable with enough certainty to support an exact-replication claim. The project therefore distinguishes:

exact replication: not defensible from surviving request provenance;
model-family replication: still limited by protocol uncertainty; and
protocol replication: feasible as a retrospective application of the recovered Dec. 24 SBS protocol to BEREC with GPT-5.4 nano.

The best-supported dated GPT-4 Turbo snapshot is gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09. Dedicated BEREC scripts use BO1B.txt, default to dry-run, require both --execute and --confirm-api-call BEREC, plan one API request, and write only under output/berec_replication/.

title: PON Governance LLM Pilot
text:
This repository contains the computational materials associated with the manuscript Institutional Rules, Boundary Objects, and LLMs — A proof-of-concept for large-N research on the governance of purpose-oriented networks.
The revised principal analysis asks:

How do contemporary OpenAI models compare with the frozen 2024 GPT-4 Turbo responses when all are evaluated under the same reconstructed step-by-step (SBS) protocol?

The historical benchmark is the preserved Dec. 24, 2024 *_sbs.txt output. The contemporary arms are the pinned GPT-5.4 nano snapshot (gpt-5.4-nano-2026-03-17) and GPT-5.6 Luna (gpt-5.6-luna). OpenAI’s Luna documentation was checked on 2026-08-31 and did not expose a dated Luna snapshot, so gpt-5.6-luna is recorded as an undated model ID together with execution-time provenance. The original 2024 outputs are never regenerated or overwritten.

title: PON Governance LLM Pilot
text:
Study cases
The strict comparison uses IRG, EUHC, cOAlition S (COAS), CAN, and CEER. BEREC remains part of the archival corpus but is handled separately because its preserved Dec. 23 output predates the final Dec. 24 request implementation.
Dedicated BEREC replication uses BO1B.txt, not BO1A.txt, and is excluded from the five-PON aggregate analysis.

title: PON Governance LLM Pilot
text:
Two linked reproductions
The repository separates two tasks:

Manuscript Table A5 replication. HBM, ASC, JNG, and the frozen legacy SBS LLM reconstruct the historical four-coder agreement table over the manuscript’s 14 prompts.
Extended SBS model comparison. The same human data and frozen legacy SBS outputs are compared with GPT-5.4 nano and GPT-5.6 Luna SBS runs over the preserved 15-question computational instrument.

Project-facing outputs use explicit agreement labels such as 3 TRUE / 1 FALSE, and report directly whether each LLM agrees with the three-human majority vote.

title: Human–LLM Comparison

title: Human–LLM Comparison
text:
BEREC auxiliary comparison
BEREC is shown separately because it is not part of the five-PON aggregate comparison and confirmed responses from HBM, ASC, and JNG are unavailable. Therefore, no HFV, human-unanimity measure, or human-reference match statistic can be computed for BEREC. The table reports only the preserved historical BEREC output, the best-evidenced December 23 GPT-4 Turbo reconstruction, and the retrospective December 24 SBS application using GPT-5.4 nano.

The BEREC table is descriptive only. The preserved historical output is not ground truth, and the December 23 GPT-4 Turbo run is a best-evidenced reconstruction rather than an exact replication. BEREC remains excluded from the 75-row five-PON totals and aggregate performance statistics reported above.
Code

Required BEREC source
All dedicated BEREC replication scripts are hard-guarded to:
input/boundary_objects/BO1B.txt
They do not use BO1A.txt for new BEREC replication calls.

Model provenance
The surviving 2024 source requested the moving alias gpt-4-turbo. It did not save the returned model identifier, request ID, system_fingerprint, or other serving metadata.
OpenAI’s current GPT-4 Turbo documentation lists gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 as the dated GPT-4 Turbo snapshot and still lists Chat Completions support. The snapshot is marked deprecated. As of 2026-08-30, it is therefore the best-supported dated snapshot for a controlled reconstruction and is still documented as callable, but the preserved Dec. 23 response itself does not prove that exact serving snapshot.
Reference: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-4-turbo

Replication claims



Table 1: BEREC replication claim levels










Level
Definition
BEREC status




Exact replication
Same exact 2024 BEREC request protocol + same exact dated snapshot
Not defensible from surviving evidence. The dated snapshot is available, but the precise Dec. 23 BEREC prompt/message state is uncertain.


Model-family replication
Same exact BEREC protocol + GPT-4 Turbo family, different snapshot
The protocol uncertainty remains, so this cannot become a strict replication merely by changing snapshots.


Protocol replication
Recovered Dec. 24 SBS protocol + GPT-5.4 nano
Feasible. This is explicitly a retrospective application of the recovered Dec. 24 SBS protocol to BEREC, not a claim about the original Dec. 23 call.






The project therefore uses the term best-evidenced Dec. 23 reconstruction for the historical-snapshot experiment.

Dedicated scripts and safeguards

Best-evidenced Dec. 23 reconstruction
Dry run; no API call:
python scripts/06_run_berec_2024_reconstruction.py
The script pins gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09, uses BO1B.txt, and reconstructs the best-evidenced early message-role layout: BEREC text as the system message and the reconstructed question prompt as the user message.
Execution requires both safeguards:
python scripts/06_run_berec_2024_reconstruction.py \
  --execute \
  --confirm-api-call BEREC


Dec. 24 SBS protocol with GPT-5.4 nano
Dry run; no API call:
python scripts/07_run_berec_sbs_current_model.py
Execute only after reviewing the dry run:
python scripts/07_run_berec_sbs_current_model.py \
  --execute \
  --confirm-api-call BEREC
Both scripts plan exactly one API request, refuse any BEREC source other than BO1B.txt, write only to a new timestamped directory under output/berec_replication/, refuse overwriting existing run directories, and never write to the preserved root-level legacy BEREC artifact.
Code

Recovered source corpus
Six archival boundary objects are retained as BO1A.txt through BO6A.txt. The five-PON strict comparison uses IRG, EUHC, COAS, CAN, and CEER. BEREC is handled separately. A second BEREC source, BO1B.txt, is the required input for the dedicated BEREC replication scripts.

Preserved model outputs
Eleven legacy response files are retained in output/:

one BEREC binary output from Dec. 23, 2024; and
ten Dec. 24, 2024 final-pipeline outputs covering five PONs under zero-shot and step-by-step prompting.

These files are historical artifacts. The repository’s execution scripts do not rewrite them.

Manuscript-facing protocol
The manuscript-facing Dec. 24 condition is the recovered prompt with the clause Let's think step by step appended. The frozen *_sbs.txt files are therefore the historical benchmark for the revised principal analysis.
The plain-zero-shot *_z.txt files remain preserved for provenance but are not the principal benchmark. The previously added improved-v1 machinery also remains in the repository as archival/secondary material and is no longer part of the primary comparison.

Instrument
The computational files contain 15 ordered binary questions. The manuscript’s Table A5 contains 14 prompts because the working-groups item (computational question 10) is omitted. The project preserves both representations:

15 questions for computational protocol fidelity; and
a 14-question manuscript subset for Table A5 replication.

Human-reference data
The authoritative human-reference file is now input/reference/legacy_human_responses_confirmed.csv. It retains the three individual human coders used in the manuscript-facing validation. Project-facing labels are:

HBM;
ASC; and
JNG.

The three-human majority vote is computed explicitly, and each LLM’s agreement with that majority is reported separately.

Table A5 audit
The surviving raw human data plus the frozen legacy SBS outputs reproduce 67 of 70 manuscript Table A5 cells. IRG prompt 3, cOAlition S prompt 8, and CEER prompt 6 reconstruct as 3-to-1 splits while Table A5 reports 2-2. These are recorded as Table A5 discrepancies relative to the surviving coder-level data, without modifying any source response.
See provenance/TABLE_A5_REPLICATION.md.

Contemporary-model extension
The primary contemporary comparison runs each registered model under the same reconstructed Dec. 24 SBS protocol for IRG, EUHC, COAS, CAN, and CEER. The registered arms are the pinned GPT-5.4 nano snapshot gpt-5.4-nano-2026-03-17 and GPT-5.6 Luna using API model ID gpt-5.6-luna. Both completed arms were executed independently and are reused by downstream analysis. The runner refuses legacy GPT-4 Turbo IDs and writes every new execution only to a new timestamped directory under output/current/.
OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Luna model page was checked on 2026-08-31. Its Snapshots section listed gpt-5.6-luna but did not expose a dated identifier analogous to gpt-5.4-nano-2026-03-17. The project therefore records gpt-5.6-luna as an undated model ID, not as a dated or immutable snapshot. The configuration stores the documentation URL and check date, and each execution preserves the UTC run timestamp plus the requested and API-returned model identifiers in its metadata and completion manifest. This is the strongest provenance currently available without inventing a snapshot that OpenAI does not expose.

BEREC caveat and dedicated workflow
BEREC’s preserved Dec. 23 response predates the final Dec. 24 request implementation. The exact request construction cannot be proven from the surviving artifacts. BEREC therefore remains outside strict five-PON aggregate comparisons and is handled only through dedicated, dry-run-by-default scripts using BO1B.txt.
See provenance/BEREC_REPLICATION.md and LEGACY_API_CALLS.md.

Analysis-integrity safeguards
The five-PON model comparison is defined as 75 decisions per model: five PONs by 15 computational questions. The comparison script fails before writing results unless it finds exactly 75 decisions for every registered model, exactly 15 decisions per model/PON, unique model/PON/question keys, exactly 75 direct legacy-versus-contemporary comparisons for each contemporary arm, and matching human-reference values across model generations.
These checks were added after an evaluation join was found to have multiplied human-reference rows across PONs. The corrected PON-specific join uses the function argument explicitly (.env$entity_slug) and the corrected comparison contains 75 decisions per model rather than 375. Under the corrected evaluation, frozen GPT-4 Turbo SBS agrees with the confirmed human reference in 86.7% of classifications and GPT-5.4 nano in 78.7%; four of the 14 GPT-4-to-GPT-5.4 changes move toward the human reference and ten move away. GPT-5.6 Luna results are computed from its completed stored run by the same checks rather than inserted manually.
